paired_full_population.scope: all requests of all 3 identical paired manifests; same request IDs
all requests of all 3 identical paired manifests; same request IDs

definitions.warm_cohort: admission in [left,right), then follow through completion; excludes censoring
definitions.category_U: sum category compute intervals / sum admitted category request residence intervals inside window
definitions.goodput: requests completing within window and passing their admission-clock SLO / window_seconds; different cohort from admission SLO
definitions.tails: nearest-rank per-seed quantiles followed by arithmetic seed mean; not pooled quantiles
definitions.classification: SS/SL/LS/LL encode total length <=80Ki vs >80Ki and miss<512 vs >=512, not absolute V/C quadrants

caveats: OD unlimited PIR and native active-group/active-path WRR borrow unused CIR; 1.25GiB/s is not a hard cap.
Once has a different static CIR allocation by category and different usable path pools, so OD-vs-Once is not a pure routing-only ablation.
Within scenario/seed the manifest is identical. Policy-dependent warm cohorts can differ; full-population paired transitions avoid this selection issue.
Full input is not strictly every-disk overloaded under every Once trajectory even though it is under all OD warm trajectories.
No per-class measured bandwidth redistribution trace is used here; static policy and class outcomes support a plausible mechanism, not a quantified attribution of every gained bandwidth unit.

od_baseline.borrowing: surplus divided by active hardware group weight, then active path weight

once.routing: per request-layer-SSU, plan each block using one pressure snapshot and local shadow projected backlog
